div.l: Ne studieth naȝt ley honde to every man
A non to drawe euery wight began
And shortly to tellen as it was
Were it by aventure or sort or cas
The soth is this þe cut fel to þe knyȝt
Of which ful blithe and glad was eủery wyȝt

Hic incipit fabula Militis
Whilom was as olde stories tellen vs
Ther was a duk þat hight Teseus
Of athenes he was lord and governour
And in his tyme suche a Conquerour
That gretter was ther non vndir þe sonne
Ful mony a rich contre hadde he wonne
What with his wysdom and his chiualrye
He conquered al the reygne of femynye
That whilome was ycleped cithia
And wedded the quene ypolita
And broȝte here home with hym into his contre
With mochel glorie ⁊and grete solempnite
And eke her yonge suster Emelye
And thus with victorie and with melodye
Late I this noble duke to athenes ride
And al his oost in armys hym be side
And certys if it nere to longe to here
I wold haue tolden fully the manere
Hownen was the reygne of femenye
By theseus and by his chiualrye
